messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: encryption-first retention option & logging window (OpsHealth)

Hi Kimberly / Sam —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the privacy requirements you flagged:

Key asks we captured from your team:
- No persistent PII storage in long-lived logs; prefer either 0-retention for PII or strong field-level masking.
- Ability to keep short-term KV/cache for session continuity (you suggested 24 hours).
- Keys must be customer-managed and regionally resident (US-east).
- Need SOC 2 + encryption-at-rest evidence and example contract language for the data handling clause.

Our suggested path forward (one pager attached):
1) Quick pilot with an \"encryption-first\" profile: PII scrubbed client-side where possible, server-side field masks applied for anything labeled PII, and a configurable KV TTL defaulted to 24h.
2) For strictly zero retention PII flows, we can enable a passthrough/headless mode where we never write logs to disk and requests are served from ephemeral memory — we call this the 0-retention route. This has limitations (no debug logs, no long-running conversations).
3) Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) are supported; we can document key residency and rotation steps.

Attachments: redwood-privacy-ttl-options.pdf (short matrix of options), opshealth-mrp-questions.docx (a few clarifying questions).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm whether 24h KV is acceptable for session continuity, or whether you need a NO-KV (0 retention) mode for specific endpoints.
- If OpsHealth wants the 0-retention mode for all user-facing calls, we'll need to scope which product features are impacted.
- I can loop in Security with a short evidence packet (SOC 2 + KMS config) and provide suggested contract language for your legal team.

If that sounds good I’ll schedule a 30-minute follow-up with our Security Engineer and Solutions lead this week.

Thanks —

Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Logan —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) 24h KV sounds acceptable for conversational continuity for product lookup flows, but not for any payloads that contain user PII. For PII we want either:
   a) 0-retention (no logs written anywhere), or
   b) Field-level tokenization/masking such that what Redwood stores is irreversibly hashed and unusable for re-identification.

2) We will need evidence of the customer-managed KMS integration working in a VPC/private deployment. OpsHealth security requires keys be in a customer-managed vault and never accessible by a service account outside our tenancy.

3) Can you provide sample contract language for a "PII non-retention" exception and a short note on feature tradeoffs if we go 0-retention? Our legal ops prefers concrete draft text.

4) SOC 2 + encryption-at-rest evidence is standard — please include the last audit date and any carveouts (if they exist). Also: any monitoring/audit log options that can be streamed to our SIEM (we'd prefer not to rely on Redwood-hosted long-term logs).

If you can get us the draft language and the security artifacts by Tuesday EOD, we can take this to our Compliance review on Wednesday.

Thanks,
Kimberly Ortiz
Head of Security & Privacy, OpsHealth
kimberly@opshealth.com | 617-555-0201

Kimberly / Sam —

Great questions — quick answers and a plan for artifacts: 

1) Field masking vs 0-retention: we can do both. For most customers we recommend a hybrid:
   - Sensitive-exempt endpoints (e.g., PHI/PII upload) can be configured for 0-retention mode. In that mode: no tokenstore writes, no disk logs, ephemeral memory only. Tradeoffs: no replay/debug, limited analytics, and certain features (e.g., long multi-turn state) are not available.
   - Non-sensitive endpoints use field-level irreversible hashing for tokens we need to persist for usage analytics; hashing is salted per-customer and keys are customer-managed where requested.

2) KMS/HSM & VPC: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and HSM-backed vaults). For Private (VPC) deployments keys stay in the customer-managed vault and Redwood requests are configured to use external key wrapping. We will document exact IAM role bindings and a diagram for your infra team. Backups: we can confirm backups and snapshots are region-restricted (US-east only) for the private deployment option.

3) Contract language: attached is a short redline we propose for a PII non-retention exception and an addendum describing pilot limits. I will also pull our Security Engineer to provide the SOC2 audit date (last completed: 2026-06-18) and any minor carveouts.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Today/Tomorrow: I’ll share a one-page MDR (mutual data requirements) and sample clause. (Attachment: redwood-privacy-ttl-options.pdf)
- Wed: 30-minute call with our Security Engineer (Neha) and Solutions Engineer (Monica) to walk the pilot and confirm KMS integration steps.
- Thu: Provide SOC 2 packet and network diagram + proposed redlined contract language for OpsHealth legal.

If that schedule works I’ll send the calendar invite for Wed at 10:00am PT.

Cheers,
